Arrows with specified endpoints

The hom and slice constructions in Section 2.1 use a common pullback of the endpoint functor. This note explains how the endpoint identifications are recovered from its matching, and how a family of arrows gives a functor into that pullback.

Write \(\operatorname {Ar}(C)=\Fun ([1],C)\) and let \(e_0,e_1\) be the two evaluation functors. For \(u,v\colon B\to C\), put \[ F(u,v)=\operatorname {Ar}(C)\times _{C\times C}B, \] where the maps to \(C\times C\) are \((e_0,e_1)\) and \((u,v)\). Denote its projections by \(a\) and \(b\), and its specified matching by \(\mu \colon (e_0,e_1)a=(u,v)b\). All categories here are absolute; a parameter category \(\Gamma \) describes a functor into these fixed categories.

Supplementary Lemma 1. The matching \(\mu \) determines specified identifications \[ p_0\colon e_0a=ub,\qquad p_1\colon e_1a=vb. \] They are obtained by projecting \(\mu \) and composing with the projection comparisons for the pairings on its two sides.

Proof idea

For the first coordinate, let \(L_0\colon \pi _1((e_0,e_1)a)=e_0a\) and \(R_0\colon \pi _1((u,v)b)=ub\) be the product comparisons, including reassociation. Then \[ p_0=R_0\cdot (\pi _1\star \mu )\cdot L_0^{-1}. \] The second coordinate has the same formula using \(\pi _2\). Here \(\star \) denotes whiskering and vertical composition applies the rightmost identification first. These formulas give the source and target frames of the universal arrow family. □

Supplementary Lemma 2. Suppose \(y\colon \Gamma \to B\) and \(A\colon \Gamma \to \operatorname {Ar}(C)\) are equipped with identifications \(s\colon e_0A=uy\) and \(t\colon e_1A=vy\). There is a functor \(\ell \colon \Gamma \to F(u,v)\), with comparisons \(a\ell =A\) and \(b\ell =y\), compatible with the specified endpoint identifications \(s,t\).

Proof idea

Write \(\kappa (f,g,r)\colon (f,g)r=(fr,gr)\) for the pairing and precomposition comparison. The cone matching determined by \(s,t\) is \[ (e_0,e_1)A \xrightarrow {\kappa (e_0,e_1,A)}(e_0A,e_1A) \xrightarrow {(s,t)}(uy,vy) \xrightarrow {\kappa (u,v,y)^{-1}}(u,v)y. \] Apply the pullback lifting operation to this cone. Its computation law compares the entire induced cone with the displayed one. In particular, it supplies both projection comparisons and their compatibility with the matching. Project that compatibility to recover the two endpoint equations. □

For absolute objects \(x,y\) of \(C\), take \(B=\star \), \(u=x\), and \(v=y\). The resulting endpoint fiber is the hom category \(\operatorname {Hom}_C(x,y)\). Taking \(B=C\), one of \(u,v\) to be the identity, and the other to be constant at a chosen object gives the corresponding slice construction. In each case, an input includes the identifications with the specified endpoints. The full lifting comparison is what permits subsequent calculations to use those same endpoints.

The normalization of the terminal parameter in the hom case is explained further in Hom expressions and restriction.
